```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {selectControl, loadWeekData, weekIssueTimeline, skillByLead, weekSkillMaps, weekIssueMaps, weekSeries} from "../assets/leads/leads.js"
pentadData = loadWeekData("../assets/pentad-leads-2023/")
geo = ({indonesia: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/indonesia.geojson").json(),
  provinces: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/provinces.geojson").json(),
  neighbours: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/neighbours.geojson").json()})
issueChoices = pentadData.issues.map(d => [d.issued, `Issued ${d.label}${d.targets.length < pentadData.leads.length ? ` (${d.targets.length} of ${pentadData.leads.length} leads in October-December)` : ""}`])
```

::: {.eyebrow}
Case 07 · Subseasonal · Pentad rainfall · Full Indonesia
:::

A pentad is CHIRPS's own shortest period: days 1-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-25 and 26
to the end of each month. This case takes the **GEFSv12** run started at 00 UTC on
**31 October 2023** and forecasts the six pentads of November, about a month ahead
in five-day steps. It is calibrated with CCA and PCR through CPT against the
**CHIRPS v3.0 pentad product** at its native 0.05° grid, 61,190 pixels over Indonesia.

CHC builds CHIRPS from pentadal and monthly totals; its daily values only share each
pentad's amount between the days, and CHC recommends pentadal or longer totals
wherever the science allows
([CHIRPS daily readme](https://data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS/v3.0/daily/readme.txt)).
So this case uses the pentad product itself. It is the same moment as the
[dekad](dekad-leads-2023.qmd) case, in half the steps. All numbers come from the
[executed notebook](../notebooks/pentad-leads-2023.ipynb).

Hover, tap or use the arrow keys on any map or chart to read values; each view can
be downloaded as it is set. Maps load when you choose them, one small file per map.

::: {.callout-note title="The short result"}
- **The forecast of 31 October leaned dry, and the first four pentads of November
  were dry**: 29 to 36 mm over Indonesia against normals of 44 to 50 mm. The forecast
  (CCA) was 35 to 41 mm, drier than normal but not as dry as observed. The last two
  pentads were near normal (45 and 49 mm) and were forecast at 43 and 47 mm.
- For every lead the most likely category (CCA) matched the observed one over less of
  the area than always forecasting the category that turned out most common, by 0.8
  to 6.6 points.
- **How far to trust each lead**, from all October-December pentads of 2000-2018:
  the area-mean CCA correlation falls from 0.30 one pentad ahead to 0.12 six pentads
  ahead. The raw GEFSv12 correlation is higher for the first three pentads (0.41,
  0.37, 0.27) and level with the calibrated one from pentad +4.
:::

## The forecast issued on 31 October 2023

A forecast is issued on the last day of a pentad, from the GEFSv12 run started at
00 UTC that day. Pentad +1 starts the next day; pentad +k starts after the k-1
pentads before it, so pentad +6 starts 26 or 27 days after the issue date and ends by
model day 34. Choose another issue date to see its targets.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof timelineIssue = selectControl("Issue date", issueChoices, "2023-10-31")
weekIssueTimeline(pentadData, timelineIssue)
```
:::

Each map is one lead against its own target, pentad +1 at the top.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mapIssue = selectControl("Issue date", issueChoices, "2023-10-31")
viewof issueMethod = selectControl("Calibration", [["CCA", "CCA"], ["PCR", "PCR"]], "CCA")
viewof issueView = selectControl("Show", [["total", "Forecast total"], ["observed", "Observed total"], ["difference", "Forecast minus observed"], ["category", "Most likely category"], ["observedCategory", "Observed category"]], "total")
weekIssueMaps(pentadData, geo, mapIssue, issueMethod, issueView)
```
:::

| Lead | Target | Forecast (mm) | Observed (mm) | 2000-2018 mean (mm) | Observed below / near / above normal (% of area) | Hit rate (%) | Reference (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pentad +1 | 1-5 Nov | 34.6 | 31.2 | 44.4 | 51.5 / 35.4 / 13.1 | 44.9 | 51.5 |
| Pentad +2 | 6-10 Nov | 35.9 | 29.1 | 44.8 | 57.0 / 33.1 / 9.9 | 56.2 | 57.0 |
| Pentad +3 | 11-15 Nov | 38.8 | 35.7 | 48.4 | 51.3 / 32.6 / 16.1 | 45.6 | 51.3 |
| Pentad +4 | 16-20 Nov | 41.1 | 32.1 | 49.8 | 65.7 / 22.1 / 12.1 | 61.2 | 65.7 |
| Pentad +5 | 21-25 Nov | 42.8 | 45.2 | 47.4 | 33.2 / 38.6 / 28.2 | 37.5 | 38.6 |
| Pentad +6 | 26-30 Nov | 46.6 | 49.0 | 51.5 | 34.6 / 36.9 / 28.4 | 33.4 | 36.9 |

: CCA forecast issued 31 October 2023, area-weighted over Indonesia. Source: [issued-2023-10-31.csv](../data/pentad-leads-2023/issued-2023-10-31.csv), which also has PCR.

- **Amounts.** The first four pentads of November were dry, 29 to 36 mm against
  normals of 44 to 50 mm. The forecast followed but stopped short (35 to 41 mm), and
  it moved closer to the normal the further ahead it looked, as a regression forecast
  does when its skill falls. The last two pentads were close to normal and so was the
  forecast, a little below the observation.
- **Categories.** For pentads +1 to +4 the forecast made below normal the most likely
  category over 85% to 87% of the area, and below normal was observed over 51% to 66%.
  The hit rate (45% to 61%) stayed under the **reference**, always forecasting the
  category that turned out most common, chosen with hindsight. For pentads +5 and +6,
  which were mixed, the forecast still favoured below normal over about two thirds
  of the area (66% and 68%).

One issue date is one outcome per lead. The next sections show how well each lead
does on average.

## How far each lead can be trusted

The calibration of each lead is trained and scored on every October-December pentad
of 2000-2018, 342 per lead. GEFSv12's hindcasts start only on Wednesdays, so each
training sample uses the one Wednesday whose start falls in a 7-day window around the
real-time offsets of that lead (1-7, 3-9, 8-14, 13-19, 18-24 and 23-29 days before the
target); the notebook checks that every 2023 offset lies inside its window.

CCA (3 predictor and 3 predictand EOFs, 2 CCA modes) and PCR (3 predictor EOFs) are
fitted through `cptcore`, the layer PyCPT's `evaluate_models` calls, with
cross-validation leaving out 35 pentads at a time (the held-out pentad and 17 on each
side, about a season). At 0.05° and 342 samples one fit took 3 to 4 hours for CCA and
43 to 49 minutes for PCR; the twelve fits ran in parallel. For every fit, CPT's
correlation map equals the correlation recomputed from its own cross-validated
hindcasts to within 0.000001.

**Pearson correlation** is 0 for no linear relationship; **2AFC** is the chance
that the forecast ranks two different pentads in the observed order, 50% for no
skill [(Mason and Weigel 2009)](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008MWR2553.1).

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof skillMetric = selectControl("Score", [["Pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["2AFC (%)", "2AFC"]], "Pearson")
skillByLead(pentadData, skillMetric)
```
:::

| Lead | CCA Pearson | PCR Pearson | Raw GEFS Pearson | CCA 2AFC (%) | PCR 2AFC (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pentad +1 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.41 | 61.0 | 61.2 |
| Pentad +2 | 0.29 | 0.30 | 0.37 | 60.5 | 60.8 |
| Pentad +3 | 0.24 | 0.24 | 0.27 | 58.9 | 59.0 |
| Pentad +4 | 0.23 | 0.23 | 0.21 | 58.6 | 58.5 |
| Pentad +5 | 0.17 | 0.18 | 0.16 | 57.0 | 57.0 |
| Pentad +6 | 0.12 | 0.13 | 0.13 | 55.5 | 55.6 |

: Area-weighted means over 61,190 pixels, 342 pentads of 2000-2018. Source: [skill-by-lead.csv](../data/pentad-leads-2023/skill-by-lead.csv).

1. **Skill falls steadily with lead**, from 0.30 to 0.12 for CCA over the six
   pentads, about a month.
2. **The raw model leads early, then calibration catches up.** GEFSv12's own anomaly
   correlates better for pentads +1 to +3 (by 0.03 to 0.12 over CCA); from pentad +4
   the two are within 0.014, CCA slightly ahead at pentads +4 and +5. The calibrated scores pay a cross-validation cost
   [(Barnston and van den Dool 1993)](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1993)006%3C0963:ADICVS%3E2.0.CO;2)
   and see the model only through 3 EOF patterns; neither effect was measured here.
3. **CCA and PCR are nearly identical**, within 0.01 at every lead.

viewof mapMetric = selectControl("Score", mapMethod === "raw" ? [["pearson", "Pearson correlation"]] : [["pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["twoafc", "2AFC"]], "pearson")

## Every issue date of late 2023

Twenty-three issue dates, from 5 September to 25 December 2023, forecast at least one
pentad of October-December; thirteen cover all six leads. One 2023 run is unusable:
the IRI Data Library's GEFSv12 forecast started on 5 December 2023 holds only missing
values, so the forecast issued that day uses the latest complete run, 4 December
00 UTC, whose offsets are one day longer and still inside every training window.

Over the 18 pentads of each lead, scored over every pixel and pentad
(area-weighted):

| Lead | Method | Hit rate (%) | Reference (%) | RPSS 2023 | RMSE 2023 (mm) | Mean forecast (mm) | Observed mean (mm) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pentad +1 | CCA | 44.7 | 48.2 | 0.08 | 25.2 | 41.3 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +1 | PCR | 45.0 | 48.2 | 0.08 | 25.2 | 41.2 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +2 | CCA | 43.5 | 48.2 | 0.07 | 25.3 | 41.2 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +2 | PCR | 43.6 | 48.2 | 0.07 | 25.5 | 41.2 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +3 | CCA | 40.9 | 48.2 | 0.04 | 26.0 | 42.1 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +3 | PCR | 41.0 | 48.2 | 0.04 | 26.0 | 41.9 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +4 | CCA | 39.4 | 48.2 | 0.03 | 26.3 | 42.8 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +4 | PCR | 39.7 | 48.2 | 0.03 | 26.4 | 42.8 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +5 | CCA | 42.6 | 48.2 | 0.05 | 25.7 | 41.9 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +5 | PCR | 42.3 | 48.2 | 0.05 | 25.9 | 41.8 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +6 | CCA | 40.0 | 48.2 | 0.02 | 26.3 | 42.2 | 35.9 |
| Pentad +6 | PCR | 40.4 | 48.2 | 0.03 | 26.3 | 42.1 | 35.9 |

: Eighteen pentads of October-December 2023, area-weighted. Observed: below normal 48.2%, near normal 32.9%, above normal 18.9% of area × pentads. Source: [ond-2023-pentad-forecasts.csv](../data/pentad-leads-2023/ond-2023-pentad-forecasts.csv).

- **Hit rate**: always forecasting "below normal" would have scored **48.2%**; every
  lead fell short of it, by 3.2 to 8.8 points.
- **RPSS 2023**, against climatological odds with the ranked probability score
  ([Epstein 1969](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1969)008%3C0985:ASSFPF%3E2.0.CO;2)),
  was positive at every lead but small (0.02 to 0.08). For one season this rewards
  leaning the right way in 2023, not skill in general.
- **The totals were too wet** on average: 41.2 to 42.8 mm per pentad against an
  observed 35.9 mm.
- **Totals below zero**: where the 2000-2018 mean plus the forecast anomaly fell
  below zero, the total was set to zero, in 3,267 to 11,766 of the 1,101,420 CCA
  pixel-pentads per lead (0.3% to 1.1%).

## Observations and anomalies

The predictand is the CHIRPS v3.0 **pentad product**, exported for Indonesia from
Earth Engine (`UCSB-CHC/CHIRPS/V3/PENTAD`) by the tutorial's
[pentad export script](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial/blob/main/research/scripts/gee/chirps3_pentad_to_drive.js)
and converted to yearly NetCDF files by
[`gee_pentad_to_netcdf.py`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial/blob/main/research/scripts/gee_pentad_to_netcdf.py),
which checks the 72 pentads of every year, the dates and the grid. Two checks in the
notebook: two pentads add up exactly to the dekadal archive (three dekads checked),
and the daily values of the weekly case, summed over each pentad, equal the pentad
product to within 0.0001 mm over all 342 training pentads.

Rainfall rises through October-December, so model and observations are turned into
**anomalies** from the 2000-2018 mean of the same calendar pentad (and, for the
model, the same lead). These means include the year held out in cross-validation;
for correlations that makes no difference (it multiplies every anomaly of a pentad by
the same factor, 19/18), and its effect inside CPT's fits was not measured. Each
forecast **total** is the observed mean plus the calibrated anomaly.

## What this does and does not show

This is one model, one set of fixed settings, 19 training years and one verifying
season, with the headline on one issue date. It shows that, for GEFSv12 pentad
rainfall over Indonesia in October-December, skill falls steadily over a month of
lead, from 0.30 to 0.12, and that calibration with these settings adds nothing to the
raw model's correlation early on and matches it later. The observations are
retrospective CHIRPS v3.0, not what was available when each forecast was issued, and
the 2023 forecasts average 31 GEFSv12 members while the hindcasts have 11.
